The world is not that boolean. Context and common sense matters.

If `Content-Security-Policy` header is missing and there is no other problem in the tested application, what is the risk? As this missing header do not provide any extra attacking scenario, you skip it? It's a second layer of defense.

> If truncation is a no-go and a hard fail according to even ASVS L1, this should be considered a major security issue.

Truncation is an issue.

Copy-paste from NIST SP 800-63B - [5.1.1.2 Memorized Secret Verifiers](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html#-5112-memorized-secret-verifiers)
_Truncation of the secret SHALL NOT be performed._

Is it major issue or minor issue, you should analyze with risk level. All is said in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1399#issuecomment-1280557323 and https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1399#issuecomment-1289051865.
